Field guide / 08—08

Make a material plan you can check

Keep dimensions, product specifications, assumptions and rounding in one note.

Vijeron · Updated 9 October 2026

Separate facts from choices

Record your measured dimensions, units, date and surface. In another column, write label figures such as coverage per litre or per box. Cut allowance and coat count are project choices; do not present them as measured facts.

Calculate in stages

Write gross area, deductions, net area, allowance or coats, and package rounding in order. This helps explain differences between a calculator result and a receipt. Save the selected brand and product number because specifications vary.

Review before buying

Recheck irregular areas, surfaces needing different colours or materials, and available pack sizes. For work involving electricity, structure or hazardous materials, follow local rules and use qualified help; this sheet only plans measurements.

Worked example

Paint note: 39.2 m² gross wall; 4.5 m² openings; 34.7 m² net; two coats; label at 10 m²/L/coat; result 6.94 L; choose can sizes after checking price and stock.

Pitfall to avoid

Do not save only '7 litres' without the measurements and product specification behind that figure.
